newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Vneshtorgbank raises capital 158 bln rbls.
newsitem.headline: Russian Vneshtorgbank raises capital 158 bln rbls.

text.p: Russia's Bank for Foreign Trade (Rosvneshtorgbank) will raise its authorised capital by 157.91 billion roubles through a bonus issue, the bank's top official said on Friday.

"The bank's supervisory council is now authorised to issue more shares in one or several issues, as the bank intends to develop and widen its operations," chairman Dmitry Tulin told a news conference.
The central bank is Vneshtorgbank's biggest shareholder.
Like other Russian banks, Vneshtorgbank shares are not actively traded.
Its pre-tax profit rose to 1.65 trillion roubles in the first eight months of 1996 from 699 billion roubles in the whole of 1995 according to Russian accounting standards, it said in a statement.
Assets fell to 24.9 trillion roubles on September 1 from 26.6 trillion on January 1, while shareholders funds rose to 6.10 trillion roubles from 3.87 trillion.
Authorised capital is currently 592.09 billion roubles.
Vneshtorgbank is Russia's second biggest bank in terms of assets and the largest custodian of Ministry of Finance bonds (MinFins).
The dollar on the Moscow Interbank Currency Exchange (MICEX) was 5,352 on August 30 and September 2. On December 29, 1995, and January 3 it was 4,640.
